subtitle: Lesson 11 · From a tracked run to a deployable version

eyebrow: The catalog deployment jobs read from
caption: Registered models listed with their latest versions — not a folder of pickled files on someone's laptop.

code:
with mlflow.start_run() as run:
    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(clf, "model")
    uri = f"runs:/{run.info.run_id}/model"
    mlflow.register_model(
        uri, "fraud-detector"
    )
caption: Each call files the run's artifact under the registered model name and auto-increments the version.

code:
client.set_registered_model_alias(
    "fraud-detector", "champion", 3
)

# a serving job resolves the alias
model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model(
    "models:/fraud-detector@champion"
)
caption: An alias is a mutable pointer — promoting a new version means moving the pointer, not the model.

eyebrow: What an alias looks like in the UI
caption: "champion" assigned to a specific version — reassigning it is instant and doesn't touch version history.
